note: Brown & Williamson internal correspondence memo, 1983 (UCSF Industry Documents, klpb0135). The previous schema covered the six routing-header fields only and explicitly deferred everything else to the text leg; that leaves the hardest and most extractable parts of the page untested. Extended with the letterhead block, the overlaid secrecy stamp, the two-column trial specification table, and the whole foot-of-page apparatus: signature initials, typist reference, document code, the RECEIVED date stamp and the Bates number. All six original fields and their values are preserved byte-for-byte, including CC as a single '; '-joined string. Every added value corroborated by 5-14 of the 14 saved engine outputs. Judgement calls: (1) the earlier note excluded the SECRET stamp as 'a notice, not a labeled field' — that decision is reversed here. It is machine-printed, sits in a different typeface overlapping the header, and a real pipeline classifying a tobacco-archive document would very much want it; it is recorded verbatim in 'security_notice'. (2) The spec table has three shapes of row: two columns of distinct values, two columns of identical values, and rows where a single centred value spans both columns while each column prints '---'. All three are represented with the same keys — 'trial_1', 'trial_2' and 'common' — with 'common' null where each trial has its own value, so an engine that silently duplicates a spanning value into both columns is distinguishable from one that reads the layout correctly. The literal '---' cell markers are preserved rather than normalised to null, because they are printed characters. (3) The Blend (%) sub-rows are split into their own array since they are a labelled sub-block with numeric values, not free-form specs. (4) The body prose and the asterisk footnote remain out of scope, as before — they are the text leg's job. (5) The RECEIVED stamp is heavily degraded; only 5 engines recover the word, but it is legible on the page above the date stamp, so it is kept. (6) New keys use snake_case; the six original keys keep their original casing (TO, CC, FROM, DATE, SUBJECT, Ref) so no dataset value or key is disturbed.

blend_percent.description: Blend (%) sub-block of the trial table, one entry per component

specifications.description: Remaining rows of the trial table, one entry per printed row

common.description: Value printed once across both columns, null when each trial has its own value
